reason: The opcodes, cycles (old 5 taken / 6 wrap, new 2: 3-4 saved) and bytes (6 -> 2, 4 saved, SKIP 4 keeps the rest in place) are right, and no caller reads C or V afterwards (checked 1050, 1842 loop's CPY, 2859 -> move_mover's SEC, 4218 -> CPX, shield rewind -> start_column PHP/PLP then SEC). But the equivalence rests on X in &40-&7F or 0, and that is false: the inputs where ORA #&40 differs (result &80-&BF) are reachable. movers_screen_address_high starts 0 (EQUB table) and update_mover moves any mover not beyond viewport_right+10, with no left bound and no requirement that it was ever placed by calculate_screen_addresses_for_mover_on_edge. From 0: subtract with a borrow gives &FF (the candidate admits this); add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX on &FF with no carry from the low byte gives &FF, N set, and its own wrap (SBC #&3F) stores &BF. A further subtract then gives &BF/&BE in the original (CMP #&40: BCS, unchanged) but &FF/&FE with ORA #&40. Concrete: a never-placed mover at 0:&00 moves left twice (&FF:&F0), right once (&F8, no carry -> &BF:&F8), left once (&BF:&F0): original X=&BF, candidate X=&FF. An enemy helicopter patrolling min..max (turns at both ends) in a never-used slot does exactly this over one patrol (40 columns left, then right: &FE+0 -> wrap &BE, ...). movers_screen_address_high is game state (passlock compares it) and the renderer places a mover by it (render.6502 list_live / world_of_address), so the state, and possibly the drawn position of a mover that reaches the view without an edge pass, differ from the original.
